what: The engine's own event times for the Sun and the Moon, held to NASA JPL's DE421 ephemeris on a broad sample. Absolute differences in seconds of Terrestrial Time, engine against reference.
reference: JPL DE421 read with jplephem 2.24 and reduced with pyerfa 2.0.1.5 to the apparent geocentric ecliptic longitude of date (light time, solar deflection, annual aberration, IAU 2006/2000A); each instant evaluated at the engine's own TT, so the differences are ephemeris and reduction only. Reference events found by a daily scan and bisection, independently of the engine.
referenceCalibration: against the 140 committed Horizons DE441 vectors inside 1900 to 2050: Sun to Saturn within 0.008 arcseconds in longitude and 0.018 in latitude; scripts and outputs in zodiacs-org/engine docs/evidence/broad-sample-2026-11-13/

moonIngresses.span: 2020 to 2031, and every 10th year from 1900 to 2050

unmatched: none: every engine event matched a reference event, apart from one Moon ingress that fell outside its year window in the comparison
